Japanese BBQ
Mar 2015 • Couples
They operate two restaurants in HCMC - Uraetai I and Uraetai II. I have only dined in Uraetai II, on Nam Ky Khoi Ngia Street. It is just a few doors from Saigon Square shopping Centre.

 A very warm restaurant that is always very busy. You will be shown to a booth to sit on bench seats. It is very comfortable and private.

At the start of the year, it extended the dining area, after taking over the Japanese restaurant, which was right next door. And yet, it is still not easy to get a table, because it is still very busy.
That in itself is a measure of its success and popularity.

It does promote the BBQ and the cuts of meat offered are a good range and all moderately priced. The BBQ pit is in the centre of the table, where the waiter drops in a hot charcoal filled brazier.

You can cook your own meats selected, but the waiter is constantly hovering and keeping a watchful eye on the meats being cooked, and will discreetly assist.

I noticed that less than half the tables order a BBQ and most order a la carte or choose from the house specials.

Delicious food with good service and not expensive.

reviews.review_text:
residentexpat
HCMC41 contributions
0
Not very Japanese
Apr 2015 • Business
My staff wanted to go to this restaurant with me for lunch as it was recommended by other Vietnamese. It may be my lack of experience in Japanese BBQ restaurants (although I have been to many authentic Japanese restaurants all over the world and have lived in Saigon for over 8 years) but I have never before been to a Japanese restaurant that had no fish on the menu (apart from some small dishes), no soy sauce, wasabi, pickled ginger on the table. The only condiments were Vietnamese fish sauce, chilli paste and chopped garlic. As I did not want to eat US beef, pork or tripe, I didn't have much choice. I ordered a stir-fried seafood set and was extremely disappointed. A few bits of shrimp and a couple of small strips of squid with vegetables stir-fried in oil with an unpleasant taste. The rice came late and was cold. The "set" otherwise consisted of a dish with one slice of tomato, one slice of cucumber and a small spoonful of kimchi, the vegetables with bottled mayonnaise on top. There was also a small dish of raw greens. I asked for Miso soup, but when it came, there was no miso that I could identify- it was grey, tasteless water with a few bits of green in it, no tofu. There was a tiny dessert (a longan jelly, loads of sugar) and coffee, but for 150,000 VND this was a massive rip-off and I left feeling very hungry. The music (repetitive boyband tunes at maximum volume) did not exactly help us have a good conversation either. 

In mitigation, I should add that the service was good and quick, but, frankly, there are so many excellent Japanese restaurants in HCMC that I would never bother coming here again, and there are plenty of BBQ options, too. My feeling was that this was a "Japanese-style" restaurant for Vietnamese, but if there were any Japanese in the kitchen I would be extremely surprised!

Great Japanese Restaurant
Sep 2014 • Friends
We noticed many locals dined here. So we thought it must be good. We tried it, and it was indeed good. Very good!

It was well decorated. Every customer has their own table, and a 'room' (sort of). The grilled 'walls' that separate tables provided some privacy.

The service was fast, efficient, and friendly. Our waiter really provided very good service. He listened to our order, repeated it, was attentive, and did it all with a smile.

The food was delicious. Pretty good Japanese food. Although, there was kimchi, which was Korean. But we noticed most places served this. Maybe it is a fad?

The deep fried chicken and tonkatsu were well prepared, crispy on the outside, and tender and juicy on the inside. The rice was one of the best we tasted, so far, in Ho Chi Minh. The miso soup as authentic as can be. Really yummy!

We took note of this place, and the many branches it has. We will definitely dine here, or at any of its branches again.

P.S. Sorry it rained heavily, and I was not able to take a photo of the shopfront.
